answer: In an agent market trading marble and umber pigment, governance votes are weighted by escrowed stake, not account count. At dawn, each ballot’s weight is computed from tokens locked for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To control a majority, an attacker must lock more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing its price risk throughout the lock.
